operation_details.item: The user prefers blunt, directive wording with minimal softening when giving graduate students feedback on draft chapters.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How is the dissertation chapter review going today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Slowly. I’m reviewing two draft chapters before the lab meeting, and both need substantial restructuring.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Are you planning to give broad comments first or mark up the arguments line by line?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’ll be direct. I want the students to know exactly what to change, so I use blunt, directive wording with very little softening.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That can make the revision plan clearer, especially when the argument or structure needs major work. Are you also coordinating the grant materials this week?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes. I have to finish the methods section, confirm the conference travel budget, and check whether the lab has ordered the new sequencing supplies.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that When I give graduate students feedback on draft chapters, I want blunt, directive wording with minimal softening—for example, 'This section is inadequate' rather than 'You might consider strengthening this area'.
